meta.purpose: Can-do statements for the Phase 7 self-assessment screen. Import each unit's `selfAssessment` object into that unit's content pack as a top-level sibling of `levels`. Do not rewrite the wording.
meta.usage: Read the statement for the level the learner just played. Never show the other two levels' wording.
meta.note: Statements are CEFR A2 'I can...' form. Easy = recognition and single words; Core = production in full sentences; Challenging = extended production, reasoning or comparison.

selfAssessment.intro: There are no right answers here. Be honest — it helps you.

vocabulary.easy: I can name some foods in English.
vocabulary.core: I can name foods and say which ones are healthy.
vocabulary.challenging: I can talk about food groups and explain my choices.

grammar.easy: I can say I like something or I don't like it.
grammar.core: I can use like, likes, don't and doesn't correctly.
grammar.challenging: I can use So do I and Neither do I to agree with someone.

listening.easy: I can hear a food word and find it.
listening.core: I can understand what someone wants to eat.
listening.challenging: I can follow a longer talk about food and catch the details.

reading.easy: I can read a short text about food.
reading.core: I can find facts in a text about food.
reading.challenging: I can understand what the writer thinks, not only what happened.

writing.easy: I can write one sentence about food.
writing.core: I can write several sentences about what I like.
writing.challenging: I can write a short diary entry with a reason.

speaking.easy: I can say what I like to eat.
speaking.core: I can ask and answer questions about food.
speaking.challenging: I can talk for a minute about food and agree with someone.

selfAssessment.notePrompt: One thing I want to get better at.

selfAssessment.intro: There are no right answers here. Be honest — it helps you.

vocabulary.easy: I can name some clothes in English.
vocabulary.core: I can name clothes and jewellery, and say what colour they are.
vocabulary.challenging: I can compare what people wear and explain why.

grammar.easy: I can say what someone is wearing.
grammar.core: I can use am, is and are with wearing, and isn't and aren't.
grammar.challenging: I can describe several people and keep singular and plural correct.

listening.easy: I can hear a clothing word and find it.
listening.core: I can understand a description of what two people are wearing.
listening.challenging: I can follow a longer description and catch the negative detail.

reading.easy: I can read a short message about clothes.
reading.core: I can find where someone is and what they are wearing.
reading.challenging: I can understand why someone describes their clothes.

writing.easy: I can write one sentence about clothes.
writing.core: I can write five sentences about me and a friend.
writing.challenging: I can describe three people and explain one choice.

speaking.easy: I can say what I am wearing.
speaking.core: I can describe what people are wearing.
speaking.challenging: I can describe and compare clothes, and say why.

selfAssessment.notePrompt: One thing I want to get better at.

selfAssessment.intro: There are no right answers here. Be honest — it helps you.

vocabulary.easy: I can name some foods and drinks in English.
vocabulary.core: I can name foods and say how they taste.
vocabulary.challenging: I can use taste words precisely and talk about where food comes from.

grammar.easy: I can say what I want.
grammar.core: I can use want and wants, and ask with does.
grammar.challenging: I can use look, smell and taste with the right endings.

listening.easy: I can hear a food or drink word and find it.
listening.core: I can understand someone ordering food.
listening.challenging: I can follow a longer description of a meal and catch how someone feels.

reading.easy: I can read a short text about food.
reading.core: I can find facts about food in a text.
reading.challenging: I can understand an opinion and a surprising detail.

writing.easy: I can write one sentence about a meal.
writing.core: I can write an order and describe how the food tastes.
writing.challenging: I can write a short review with a reason.

speaking.easy: I can say what I want to eat.
speaking.core: I can order politely and ask how something tastes.
speaking.challenging: I can describe a meal using all three senses.

selfAssessment.notePrompt: One thing I want to get better at.

selfAssessment.intro: There are no right answers here. Be honest — it helps you.

vocabulary.easy: I can name some classes and school things.
vocabulary.core: I can name classes, school objects and days of the week.
vocabulary.challenging: I can talk about what I carry to school and explain why.

grammar.easy: I can say what I have.
grammar.core: I can use have and has, and don't and doesn't have.
grammar.challenging: I can use have and has correctly even in negatives and questions.

listening.easy: I can hear a class word and find it.
listening.core: I can understand someone talking about their timetable.
listening.challenging: I can follow a longer description and catch the reason behind it.

reading.easy: I can read a short note about school things.
reading.core: I can find facts in a note about school.
reading.challenging: I can understand why a bag is heavy and what that tells me.

writing.easy: I can write one sentence about a class.
writing.core: I can fill a chart about my classes and what I need.
writing.challenging: I can write a paragraph about my week with reasons.

speaking.easy: I can say one class I have.
speaking.core: I can ask and answer questions about classes.
speaking.challenging: I can describe my week and explain which class is hardest.

selfAssessment.notePrompt: One thing I want to get better at.

selfAssessment.intro: There are no right answers here. Be honest — it helps you.

vocabulary.easy: I can name some rooms and things in a house.
vocabulary.core: I can name objects and the places in a house and garden.
vocabulary.challenging: I can talk about where things belong and why.

grammar.easy: I can say where one thing is.
grammar.core: I can use Where is and Where are, and It's and They're.
grammar.challenging: I can keep the question, the short answer and the full answer the same number.

listening.easy: I can hear an object word and find it.
listening.core: I can understand where something is.
listening.challenging: I can follow a longer description and catch a negative.

reading.easy: I can read a short note about where things are.
reading.core: I can find where things are in a note.
reading.challenging: I can understand a joke or an aside in a note.

writing.easy: I can write one sentence with in, on or under.
writing.core: I can fill a chart showing where things are.
writing.challenging: I can describe a room and give reasons.

speaking.easy: I can tell someone where my things are.
speaking.core: I can ask and answer Where is and Where are.
speaking.challenging: I can describe a room for a minute.

selfAssessment.notePrompt: One thing I want to get better at.

selfAssessment.intro: There are no right answers here. Be honest — it helps you.

vocabulary.easy: I can name some weather words.
vocabulary.core: I can name the weather and the right clothes for it.
vocabulary.challenging: I can talk about climates and explain why people dress differently.

grammar.easy: I can say It's hot or It's cold.
grammar.core: I can ask Is it...? and use Put on and Don't put on.
grammar.challenging: I can give instructions and refuse them with the right verb form.

listening.easy: I can hear a weather word and find it.
listening.core: I can understand a weather report.
listening.challenging: I can follow a report that compares two places.

reading.easy: I can read a short text about the weather.
reading.core: I can find facts about the weather in a place.
reading.challenging: I can understand why two opposite climates share one name.

writing.easy: I can write one sentence about the weather.
writing.core: I can write what to wear in each kind of weather.
writing.challenging: I can write a weather report with an instruction.

speaking.easy: I can say what the weather is like today.
speaking.core: I can say what to wear and what not to wear.
speaking.challenging: I can give a one-minute weather report.

selfAssessment.notePrompt: One thing I want to get better at.

selfAssessment.intro: There are no right answers here. Be honest — it helps you.

vocabulary.easy: I can name some things people do in a season.
vocabulary.core: I can name activities for each season.
vocabulary.challenging: I can compare seasons and explain which I prefer.

grammar.easy: I can say what I do in a season.
grammar.core: I can use he, she and it with -s for seasonal activities.
grammar.challenging: I can use goes and does correctly, and keep Neither...nor singular.

listening.easy: I can hear a season activity and find it.
listening.core: I can understand what people do in each season.
listening.challenging: I can follow a text that compares places in one country.

reading.easy: I can read a short text about seasons.
reading.core: I can find what people do in each season.
reading.challenging: I can understand why a text is organised the way it is.

writing.easy: I can write one sentence with in the and a season.
writing.core: I can fill a chart about the seasons.
writing.challenging: I can write a paragraph comparing seasons with a reason.

speaking.easy: I can say one thing I do in summer.
speaking.core: I can talk about all four seasons.
speaking.challenging: I can give a one-minute talk about the year.
